deviations: Y1, the largest. I did not adopt V2's repair (B) as given. I kept its material-first order, and in place of the index, before the turn, I place a cleaned part from the centre of every kept part, |q| then q in RANK_Q. In code: acrossTies writes that place into keys 3-6, and the comparator ranks kept parts first and orders cleaned parts by material, then keys 3-15. Reasons, measured. (B)'s premise that the index's split 'moves no mass, COM or balance' is false for sampled overlaps: ids moved the mass by 2.05e-4 kg on a Ctrl+D build of two Dust Balls, and the COM by 2.4e-6 on V1's csids. With the turn ahead of position, a Z mirror image moved the mass of the editor's mirror copies by 1.2e-6 to 1.44e-6 kg, where f7ac37d did not. Both are regressions against f7ac37d on editor-reachable inputs, of the major's kind. My first form (B2, index only replaced) kept the turn flip. The adopted form keeps everything (B) was chosen for: no hidden part steers, whole-design moves are exact, and twins of different materials stay mirror-invariant. It is round 3's byte for byte on every corpus and on every mirror image dumped. Consequently §4.3 states no 'one place an id decides', because none remains; it says why the index and the turn were not used.

Y2. The hidden-ownership pin also moves a box of two Iron fillers 0.05 down Z; otherwise V1's world-planes mutant passes it. Two pins were added for the adopted form: ids along Z, and the mirror copies.
